base_member_text: [L20-L21] (MED/pointer/ownership) The code assumes every associated space pointer owns a deallocatable target, but the pointer-based state model does not express or check that ownership contract.
audit_member_text: [L20] (MED/pointer-ownership) The code treats ASSOCIATED as proof that the pointer owns a deallocatable target, although an associated pointer can legally reference a target it does not own unless that ownership invariant is enforced elsewhere.

base_member_text: [L17-L22] (MED/allocation/data-loss) Reallocation deallocates the old target before allocating the new one, discarding all prior values and leaving no recovery path if allocation fails.
audit_member_text: [L17-L22] (MED/allocation/error-handling) Reallocation destroys the existing target before attempting an unchecked allocation, so allocation failure loses the prior data and is not surfaced through STAT.

adversarial.rationale: An associated array target is indeed discarded before an allocation without STAT, so allocation failure is fatal and there is no rollback. The existing MPI callers use this on the output process to size output buffers (varianceupdate.F90:84-90) or immediately collect replacement values (spaceparams.F90:1094-1125); preserving their old contents is not their contract, so the supported issue is LOW allocation-failure robustness rather than loss of authoritative simulation data.
